sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Direct bachelor-to-PhD possible; expected preparation includes one year each of abstract algebra and analysis
(real/complex). UChicago degree meets institutional degree type. [s1] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Prepare a mathematics-course abstract, preferably with textbooks, and identify fit with the department's
research areas. [s1]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior supervisor agreement is listed; the department emphasizes matching its research strengths. Spencer
Leslie specifically invites prospective graduate students to email him and offers virtual meetings during his
2026-27 IAS visit. [s1] [b18]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use MCGS application, not documents sent to mathematics. Submitted-file processing/status help appears in
central FAQ. [s2] [s3]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Standing admissions rules; explicit 2027 calendar and stipend not verified. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application; Funding consideration [Standing rule]
January 20 for full admission/TA consideration, standing annual date; 2027 and cutoff time/time zone not
expressly stated. [s1]
Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]

allowance. Final official transcripts due July 15 after acceptance. [s2]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
PhD reply-by date: April 15 (standing annual rule; verify 2027 offer). [s3]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
If needed: TOEFL 100 / new-scale 5.0, IELTS 7.0 or DET 130; official scores, valid two years. [s2]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Eligible through US degree or two academic years of full-time US study before BC. Official transcript clears the
requirement; qualifying unofficial records permit review meanwhile. [s2]

GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Neither GRE appears in the current mathematics required-items list. Whether optional scores are considered is
not stated. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three, preferably undergraduate mathematics instructors; one additional letter allowed centrally. [s1] [s2]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Standard aid review is automatic with admission application; no separate aid application or additional
reference listed. [s4]
What sends the invitation; Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Register referees while completing application; letters may arrive after applicant submission. Exact invitation
trigger is not published. Interfolio accepted via gsasinfo@bc.edu after completing Recommendations. [s2]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Applicant status portal tracks received materials; exact letter-specific display is not explained publicly. [s3]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Reapplicants need a new application and supporting documents. Across different MCGS programs,
transcripts/scores may be shared; do not presume letters transfer. Updates to submitted letters unspecified.
[s3]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Tuition scholarship and stipend paid over 9 academic-year months. Mathematics annual dollar amount and
summer guarantee not published in reviewed pages. [s1]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Anticipated five-year support, contingent on progress and TA/TF performance. [s1]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
MCGS explicitly includes domestic and international students in assistantship, fellowship and scholarship
support. [s4]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
First-year TA, then usually TF; approximately 15 hours/week. Weekly teaching seminar required. [s1]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Standard aid review is automatic with admission application; no separate aid application or additional
reference listed. [s4]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
University fellowships, research assistantships and faculty grant support; specific amounts/eligibility vary. [s4]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 75, nonrefundable per application. [s3]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Upload documented hardship request inside application, then submit. Only MCGS admissions grants waivers.
Current students should obtain financial-aid officer documentation; exchange-rate/payment difficulty alone
insufficient. [s2]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Dawei Chen
Moduli of curves/differentials, with connections to Teichmüller dynamics. [s5]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.

Research evidence: 2026 · Isoresidual curves
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Qile Chen
Logarithmic geometry, stable maps, rational connectedness and enumerative geometry. [s6]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2025 · Punctured logarithmic maps
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Maksym Fedorchuk
Moduli spaces, geometric invariant theory, stability of fibrations. [s7]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2022; newer 2024 works listed in preparation · Stability of fibrations over one-dimensional bases
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Brian Lehmann
Birational geometry and rational curves on Fano varieties; geometric Manin conjectures, positivity and rational
points. [a14] [a14p]
Current departmental faculty; accepting new doctoral students is not confirmed publicly.
Research evidence: 2026 · Optimal bounds in Bend-and-Break
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Number theory
Benjamin Howard
Arithmetic geometry, cycles on unitary Rapoport-Zink spaces, arithmetic intersection formulas, local Whittaker
functions and Hecke correspondences. [s1] [s8] [s9] [q13]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Arithmetic Siegel-Weil for the spherical Hecke algebra
Research-paper evidence. Publication year is as stated; an old paper is not proof of recent activity.
Dubi Kelmer
Analytic number theory and homogeneous dynamics, quadratic forms, quantitative Diophantine approximation
and rational points. [b24] [b24p]
Current faculty; accepting new doctoral students is not publicly confirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 · Effective density of values of indefinite ternary inhomogeneous quadratic forms
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Robert Gross
Algebraic number theory and Frobenius statistics; the verified later paper studies lattice sphere packing and
eutactic quadratic forms. [b26] [b26p]
Current faculty; accepting new doctoral students is not publicly confirmed.
Research evidence: 2022 journal volume; online June 2019 · Lattice-Packing by Spheres and Eutactic Forms
Publisher metadata verifies this later paper. No newer research paper was established; university profile itself lists older work.
Confirm current project and supervision activity.

Representation theory
Xin Jin
Microlocal sheaf theory, symplectic geometry and their categorical connections. [s10] [s12]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2024 · Brane structures in microlocal sheaf theory
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
David Treumann
Sheaves, mirror symmetry and geometric representation theory. [s11] [s12]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2024 · Brane structures in microlocal sheaf theory
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Mark Reeder
Representation theory of p-adic and Lie groups, Weyl-group characters, zero-weight spaces, Hecke algebras
and Langlands parameters. [b28] [b28p]
Current faculty; accepting new doctoral students is not publicly confirmed.
Research evidence: 2024 journal volume; online May 2022 · Weyl Group Characters Afforded By Zero Weight Spaces
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Arithmetic geometry
Keerthi Madapusi
Arithmetic geometry, integral models of Shimura varieties, p-adic Hodge theory, p-divisible groups and derived
or prismatic methods. [b16] [b16p]
Current faculty; accepting new doctoral students is not publicly confirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint, updated May 23 · On canonicity for integral models for Shimura varieties with hyperspecial
level
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Representation theory / number theory
Spencer Leslie
Automorphic, p-adic and geometric representation theory; relative and metaplectic Langlands, trace formulas,
endoscopy and Hitchin fibrations. [b18] [b18p]
Associate Professor; at IAS as a Von Neumann Fellow in 2026-27. Explicitly welcomes email from prospective graduate students
and offers virtual meetings while away.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · Relative Hitchin fibrations and endoscopy for Unitary Friedberg-Jacquet varieties
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Number theory / representation theory
Solomon Friedberg
Automorphic representations, functoriality, metaplectic groups, L-functions and Shimura correspondences.
[b20] [b20p]
Current faculty; accepting new doctoral students is not publicly confirmed.

Research evidence: 2026 · On the cubic Shimura lift to PGL(3): The fundamental lemma
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Number theory / arithmetic geometry
Avner Ash
Galois representations attached to arithmetic-group homology, Hecke eigenclasses, modular symbols and
Serre-type conjectures. [b22] [b22p]
Current faculty; accepting new doctoral students is not publicly confirmed.
Research evidence: November 2025 author version; published 2026 · Sums of two irreducible Galois representations and the
homology of GL_n(Z)
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.

Boston College
United States · Mathematics PhD
Roster and rank verification handled separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• English waiver may remain visibly pending until official transcript arrives without blocking review.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Direct bachelor-to-PhD possible; expected preparation includes one year each of abstract algebra and analysis
(real/complex). UChicago degree meets institutional degree type. [s1] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Prepare a mathematics-course abstract, preferably with textbooks, and identify fit with the department's
research areas. [s1]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior supervisor agreement is listed; the department emphasizes matching its research strengths. Spencer
Leslie specifically invites prospective graduate students to email him and offers virtual meetings during his
2026-27 IAS visit. [s1] [b18]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use MCGS application, not documents sent to mathematics. Submitted-file processing/status help appears in
central FAQ. [s2] [s3]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Standing admissions rules; explicit 2027 calendar and stipend not verified. [s1] [s2]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application; Funding consideration [Standing rule]
January 20 for full admission/TA consideration, standing annual date; 2027 and cutoff time/time zone not
expressly stated. [s1]
Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
All application materials due at program deadline (January 20 standing date); no published separate late-letter
allowance. Final official transcripts due July 15 after acceptance. [s2]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
PhD reply-by date: April 15 (standing annual rule; verify 2027 offer). [s3]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
If needed: TOEFL 100 / new-scale 5.0, IELTS 7.0 or DET 130; official scores, valid two years. [s2]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Eligible through US degree or two academic years of full-time US study before BC. Official transcript clears the
requirement; qualifying unofficial records permit review meanwhile. [s2]

GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Neither GRE appears in the current mathematics required-items list. Whether optional scores are considered is
not stated. [s1] [s2]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
All postsecondary transcripts, including summer/nondegree/study-abroad work. Central rules accept unofficial
copies for review. [s2] [s3]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
Mathematics-course abstract required; textbooks helpful. No public length, format or upload category
specified. [s1]
Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Course abstract requested; detailed syllabus requirements not stated. [s1]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three, preferably undergraduate mathematics instructors; one additional letter allowed centrally. [s1] [s2]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Standard aid review is automatic with admission application; no separate aid application or additional
reference listed. [s4]
What sends the invitation; Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Register referees while completing application; letters may arrive after applicant submission. Exact invitation
trigger is not published. Interfolio accepted via gsasinfo@bc.edu after completing Recommendations. [s2]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Applicant status portal tracks received materials; exact letter-specific display is not explained publicly. [s3]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Reapplicants need a new application and supporting documents. Across different MCGS programs,
transcripts/scores may be shared; do not presume letters transfer. Updates to submitted letters unspecified.
[s3]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume; Personal / background statement; Research proposal; Writing sample /
thesis / research summary; Publications list; Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]
Statement of purpose [Conflict]
Department advises explaining research-area fit in SOP; central guidance suggests 1-2 pages on preparation,
motivation and goals (paraphrase). Mathematics checklist omits SOP: confirm portal requirement. Formatting
unspecified. [s1] [s2]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Describe fit in SOP with number/representation theory, algebraic geometry or geometry/topology/dynamics; no
separate research statement listed. [s1]

Course-list document [Standing rule]
Mathematics-course abstract required; textbooks helpful. No public length, format or upload category
specified. [s1]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
Standard aid review is automatic with admission application; no separate aid application or additional
reference listed. [s4]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Tuition scholarship and stipend paid over 9 academic-year months. Mathematics annual dollar amount and
summer guarantee not published in reviewed pages. [s1]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Anticipated five-year support, contingent on progress and TA/TF performance. [s1]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
MCGS explicitly includes domestic and international students in assistantship, fellowship and scholarship
support. [s4]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
First-year TA, then usually TF; approximately 15 hours/week. Weekly teaching seminar required. [s1]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Standard aid review is automatic with admission application; no separate aid application or additional
reference listed. [s4]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
University fellowships, research assistantships and faculty grant support; specific amounts/eligibility vary. [s4]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 75, nonrefundable per application. [s3]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Upload documented hardship request inside application, then submit. Only MCGS admissions grants waivers.
Current students should obtain financial-aid officer documentation; exchange-rate/payment difficulty alone
insufficient. [s2]
Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
Department asks for official transcripts; central MCGS explicitly accepts unofficial copies at application.
Department discusses SOP, but central math checklist omits it. [s1] [s2]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm 2027 date/time, SOP requirement, annual stipend/summer/insurance, referee receipt/replacement
mechanics and optional-paper uploads. [s1] [s2] [s3]
